title: The Second Law of Thermodynamics
lead: Two blocks at different temperatures, sealed off from the rest of the universe, exchange heat until they agree. Following their entropy on the way gives a criterion for spontaneity, which is then extended to systems that exchange heat with their surroundings.
notes: The page prints no credits; its sketch of the two blocks and its graph of entropy against time are folded into one moving simulation.
exercise_notes: The book sets no exercise here; the one exercise is new and AI-written, its answers computed. Numeric answers accept a 2% tolerance.

exercises.source_id: two identical blocks of metal, say aluminum
exercises.prompt:
Two identical aluminium blocks, each with $\kCV = 10.0$ J/K, start at 400 K and 300 K. They are put in contact and isolated from everything else.

  1. What temperature do they reach?
  2. What is the entropy change of the hotter block?
  3. What is the entropy change of the pair?

parts.hint: The block cools at constant heat capacity from 400 K to the final temperature.

answer.solution:
a. The blocks are identical, so the energy one loses the other gains and they meet at the average, $(400 + 300)/2 = 350$ K.

b. $\Delta S_A = \kCV\ln\dfrac{350}{400} = (10.0)(-0.1335) = -1.335$ J/K.

c. The colder block gains $\kCV\ln\dfrac{350}{300} = +1.542$ J/K, so the pair gains $-1.335 + 1.542 = 0.206$ J/K, which is $\kCV\ln\dfrac{(400 + 300)^2}{4(400)(300)} = 10.0\ln\dfrac{490000}{480000}$. It is positive, as the second law requires.

footnotes.html: The book prints $\kTA^2 + \kTB^2$ in the numerator; it is $(\kTA + \kTB)^2$. The printed form can fall below $4\kTA\kTB$: at 400 K and 300 K it gives $\Delta S = \kCV\ln(250000/480000) = -0.652\,\kCV$, a decrease, where $(\kTA + \kTB)^2$ gives $+0.0206\,\kCV$.

derivations.what: the entropy produced as heat flows between the blocks

assumes.text: There is only one path (along $\kq$), so we do not need to worry about reversible and irreversible paths: the heat that flows is the reversible heat.

nodes.note: The book says that because $U$ is a state function this makes $q$ a state function as well. Heat stays a path function; with no work, $\delta q_A$ equals $dU_A$ along the one path open here, which is all the argument needs.

then.why: Each block takes in its energy at its own temperature, and the entropy changes of the two blocks add.

derivations.what: the entropy change of two identical blocks

assumes.text: Each block has the same heat capacity $\kCV$, so its energy changes by $\kCV$ times its change in temperature.
Heating or cooling a block of constant heat capacity $\kCV$ from $T_i$ to $T_f$ changes its entropy by $\kCV\ln(T_f/T_i)$.
The entropy changes of the two blocks add.

steps.cap: A sum of logarithms is the logarithm of the product: $\ln x + \ln y = \ln xy$.
